messages:
Maya Patel: Quick question — I'm putting together a proposal for header-based routing at the gateway. Goal: allow tenant pinning via a custom header and fall back to auth context when header missing. Rough idea: prefer `X-Redwood-Tenant` (canonicalized to lower-case), then JWT claim `tenant_id`, else default pool. Any red flags?

Sam Huang: Sounds reasonable. A few things: 1) don't rely on `Authorization` header raw — parse JWT upstream and use a normalized claim. 2) canonicalize header names to avoid case-sensitivity bugs (lowercase keys). 3) define explicit precedence and a clear audit log for overrides.

Liam O'Connor: Also: please don't use `User-Agent` for routing. It's spoofable and noisy. Only ok for lightweight experiments where spoofing isn't an issue.

Kai Zhang: Telemetry note: if we tag traces with tenant header values, we must hash or redact to avoid PII leakage. Add a config flag to enable full-value tagging for customers who opt in and have DPA.

Maya Patel: Good calls. For the console UX I was thinking: a toggle on the route that lets you choose match type: `header` vs `jwt-claim` vs `composite` and UI shows effective precedence. Also an "admin override" checkbox that forces routing to a specific backend for debugging. Should we allow that?

Sam Huang: Admin override is handy but needs strict audit logs and a quick rollback button. Also the override should be implemented as a higher-precedence rule (not a mutation of existing rules) so we can show the diff in the rollout UI.

Maya Patel: Example of the rule YAML I'm proposing (edge gateway):

```yaml
routes:
  - match:
      header:
        name: x-redwood-tenant
        exact: tenant-acme
    backend: acme-pool
  - match:
      jwt:
        claim: tenant_id
        regex: ^tenant-(.*)
    backend: ${claim_match}
  - match:
      default: true
    backend: shared-pool
```

Sam Huang: Nice. A couple of implementation notes: - normalize header names (lowercase) in the matcher. - add an explicit `strip_headers` list for security-sensitive headers (never forward Authorization to backend). - support `transform` to rewrite header values for backends that expect a different header name.

Liam O'Connor: For auth propagation: we should propagate a signed short-lived header (edge signs with our key) rather than raw JWT, so backends can trust it without re-verifying. That also limits surface area for stolen tokens.

Kai Zhang: Ops: add a telemetry dimension `route_match_reason` with values like `header:x-redwood-tenant`, `jwt:tenant_id`, `default`. That makes rollout metrics easy. But for privacy, store raw header values only in ephemeral logs and hashed in long-term metrics.

Maya Patel: Who wants to own the PR? Needs: gateway matcher change, console UX toggle, telemetry tag, e2e tests, docs. ETA: two sprints?

Sam Huang: I'll take the gateway matcher and e2e tests. Will open a draft PR and drop the config snippet in the description.

Liam O'Connor: I'll do the signed-propagation plan and a small PoC for the edge signer.

Kai Zhang: I'll add telemetry and privacy docs (masking rules, opt-in). Also will add suggested dashboards: per-tenant latency, error-rate, and route-match breakdown.

deploy-bot: deploy:gateway-config-v2 feature/headers-routing opened by Sam Huang — CI started :rocket:

Maya Patel: :thumbsup: thanks all. Sam — when you open the PR, can you include a tiny sample of the console screen mock so product can review the UX?

Sam Huang: yep, will attach a quick Figma frame and the YAML.

Liam O'Connor: One last thing — add unit tests for header-case, and a test to assert JWT fallback triggers when header absent. Saves a lot of debugging later.

Maya Patel: Agreed. Closing loop: we'll add audit-log entries for any admin override and a 1-click revert. Will sync with security before merging.

Kai Zhang: :eyes: ping me if you need dashboard query help.

Sam Huang: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/412 (draft)

Maya Patel: Great. Let's keep discussion on the PR for design/code specifics.
